text:
jen: paging oncall — seeing repeated pod evictions in the preproc/tokenizer tier, nodes reporting kernel OOMs; customer errors spiking. graphs -> https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123
ops-bot: [ALERT] preproc-pool CPU p95 > 98% for >2m on pool=tokenize-prod; node=k8s-preproc-12 kernel OOM events=3
samir: I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking recent deploys. can someone post customer impact?
maria: support: a small subset of chat requests returned 500s starting ~2026-07-15T01:09Z (approx). quick triage says failures correlate to preproc latency/timeouts. CS pinged.
devon: looks like a single tokenizer worker thread is spinning — high syscalls and continuous reallocs. suspect runaway regex or pathological prompt.
samir: initial container stderr snippet:
```
E0715 01:11:58 tokenizer/worker.go:312] tokenize: growing buffer: 1.2MB -> 48MB
runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 65536 bytes
panic: runtime: out of memory\n```
jen: yikes. mitigation options: 1) cordon node k8s-preproc-12 and drain to stop repeated evictions; 2) temporarily reduce max-concurrency on router for preproc; 3) set per-request tokenizer caps (hotfix env) to fail fast.
devon: hotfix ready: env TOKENIZER_MAX_TOKENS=50000 and TOKENIZER_LOOP_GUARD=1 will abort abusive requests. I'll stage.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout start preproc/tokenizer hotfix by devon @ 2026-07-15T01:17Z
samir: also saw a CUDA error earlier on a different node: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` — looks unrelated (GPU node), but noted.
maria: I'm drafting customer note: "We observed intermittent 500s for requests processed by the tokenizer service between 01:09–01:22 UTC. Root cause was a tokenizer pre-processing loop exhausting CPU and memory on affected pods; mitigations applied." Will push when we have stable rollback. :pencil2:
jen: immediate action taken: cordoned k8s-preproc-12, drained impacted pods; scaled preproc-replicaset from 5 -> 8 to absorb in-flight work; applied TOKENIZER_MAX_TOKENS to prod.
oncall-amy: I'm taking over the page at 01:22 UTC for monitoring and follow-up (30m watch). handoff notes: keep token caps, watch p95 latency and node OOM count.
devon: quick log from restarted pod shows tokenizer aborting with clear error now instead of looping — good sign.
samir: applying router-level backpressure: set route.preproc.queue_depth=8 and route.preproc.concurrency=4 to reduce parallelism.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: hotfix rollout succeeded, all preproc pods healthy (8/8) @ 01:30Z
maria: customer-impact: approximately 0.25% of requests returned 500; for ~1,200 requests we applied a best-effort retry/fallback to a lighter model, CS notified customers in impacted segment.
jen: next steps (post-incident): file PR to add tokenizer loop-detection guard (fail-fast), add an alert for repeated realloc pattern, add a unit test for pathological prompt, and evaluate whether per-request CPU limits are needed. assigning owners.
devon: filed PR #4520 "tokenizer: add loop-detection and early-exit" and linked to incident.
incident-bot: Incident updated — severity=high, status=investigating -> mitigated, linked runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/example-tokenize-loop
oncall-amy: handoff complete to oncall-amy; will monitor for another 15m then move to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
maria: creating action items in tracker: INC-4520 (devon), INC-4521 (ops — improve node selection), INC-4522 (sre — add alert).
samir: note: please correlate with CUDA error earlier (node preproc-gpu-03) to ensure not a wider pattern.
jen: thanks all — great cross-team response. will publish incident summary once postmortem is drafted.
